To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of SCM and corrosion inhibitors to concrete mixtures can reduce the chloride permeability of concrete, and the laboratory tests used to measure concrete durability are effective in predicting the performance of the concrete mixtures in the field.

(1) the addition of SCM to concrete mixtures improves the durability characteristics of the concrete by decreasing the porosity of concrete and reducing the chloride ingress, (2) the use of chemical inhibitors, such as corrosion inhibitors and shrinkage reducing admixtures, improves the durability characteristics by decreasing the chloride ingress and increasing the resistance of concrete to chloride penetration, and (3) laboratory tests such as rapid chloride permeameter test and sorptivity test can be used to predict the durability of
the addition of fly ash, slag and corrosion inhibitor to the concrete mixtures can reduce the diffusion of chlorides into concrete, and thus, the risk of corrosion of the reinforcing steel.

the development and evaluation of a methodology for field validation of the concrete transport properties.
the field validation of concrete transport property measurement methods.
the evaluation of concrete properties and their durability performance in the laboratory and field.

the laboratory tests were able to predict the field results for all the concrete mixtures tested.

the use of SCMs and/or corrosion inhibitors can improve the durability of concrete.
